Subject: Follow-up: inbound/outbound telemetry scrubbing Q&A

Hi Alex / Maya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the pieces we said we would follow up on for Medicus' telemetry/logging constraints:

- Scope: you want request/response capture for debugging but need guaranteed removal or masking of any PHI/PII fields (names, MRNs, SSNs, phone, email) from logs stored in our systems.
- Residency: logs must be retained only in us-east-1 and be exportable to your S3 bucket under your KMS.
- Trace identifiers: you use a 128-bit trace ID in headers; you want the header preserved for distributed tracing but obfuscated in any debug snapshot to a one-way token so customer-identifying correlation is not possible.
- Retention: default debug snapshots no older than 30 days; audit stream (metadata-only) for 365 days.

Action items we committed to:
1) Provide a concrete proposal of the masking approach for headers + request/response bodies.
2) Share an example redaction snapshot and a short checklist mapping which header keys will be replaced vs allowed.
3) Confirm the export flow to your S3 and KMS integration steps.

Attaching a short technical snapshot that shows the masking controls (will send the full checklist after the team review). Let us know if the summary above missed anything.

Thanks,
Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inbound/outbound telemetry scrubbing Q&A

Camila — thanks for the recap. That aligns well. Couple of clarifying Qs before we go deep: 

1) Can you confirm whether request/response snapshots created for triage are stored encrypted at rest with customer-controlled keys or are they encrypted with Redwood-managed keys? We specifically need to avoid provider-managed keys for any full payload snapshots.

2) For trace ID obfuscation: we want to be able to correlate across our services and Redwood for tracing, but cannot allow reversible mapping on your side. Is the one-way tokenization you mentioned HMAC-based with a salt we control, or a deterministic hash?

3) For headers: we have custom headers X-MEDICUS-USER and X-SESSION-ORIG; are you able to provide a policy table that indicates which headers are auto-stripped, which are masked, and which may be proxied unchanged?

Also please send the checklist in Excel if possible — Legal will want to attach that to the review packet.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Director, Security & Compliance | Medicus Health
security@medicus.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <security@medicus.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inbound/outbound telemetry scrubbing Q&A

Alex —

Short answers up front:
- Snapshot encryption: full payload snapshots (what you called "triage snapshots") can be configured to use customer KMS in your AWS account via our cross-account export pipeline. That means keys are customer-controlled and Redwood never persists the unencrypted blob.

- Trace ID obfuscation: we propose a deterministic, one-way hash (SHA-256 truncated) salted with a per-customer nonce that you provide during onboarding. The salt is kept in your KMS as an encrypted parameter; Redwood receives only the hashed value. This lets you correlate on the hashed value while preventing us from reversing to the original trace ID. If you prefer HMAC with a key you manage, we support that too as an alternative.

- Headers: we've got a policy engine that supports three actions per header: allow (pass-through), mask (replace payload with "[MASKED]" or a hashed token), drop (strip entirely). Attached is a draft mapping for the meds you called out; we can make it into a canonical checklist.

I'll loop in the infra team for the S3 export docs; Camila, I'll send a short runbook and the template for the S3 IAM role after the thread.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inbound/outbound telemetry scrubbing Q&A

Alex — adding a compliance note from our side: 

- Retention windows: we will implement two retention classes for artifacts: 
  * debug_snapshot (payload-permitted) — configurable up to 30 days by default for your account; exports to your S3 must happen before automatic deletion.
  * audit_metadata (headers + metadata only) — 365 days, stored encrypted, and accessible via our audit API.

- Access controls: all access to debug_snapshot artifacts is RBAC-gated and logged; we can provide an audit trail (S3 access log + Redwood access events) for any retrievals.

Please confirm those windows are acceptable and whether Legal needs any additional documentation (SOC2 SOC 3 artifacts, data flow diagrams).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Staff Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Best,
